newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ /United alliance begins.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ /United alliance begins.

text.p: The alliance between United Airlines and Air New Zealand began on Thursday with an early morning flight between Auckland and Melbourne, Air New Zealand said.
The United Airlines Boeing 747-400 aircraft departed Auckland at 7.05 a.m. carrying passengers from both airlines.
The code-sharing arrangement, which was announced late last year, covers 130 flights a week operated by the two carriers.
"This alliance brings benefits for both airlines but, as importantly, it enhances tourism for this country," Air New Zealand managing director Jim McCrea said.

"United Airlines is the world's largest carrier and this code-sharing arrangement marks a real breakthrough in terms of our ability to develop the vital North American tourism market, and to extend and improve the services we can offer Australian and New Zealand travellers to the United States and beyond."
He said that from Thursday, the core-share arrangement means Air New Zealand's international network effectively expands to include Chicago and San Francisco.
"We are looking to increase the number of American cities included in the code-share arrangement and will be working closely with United Airlines to develop this," McCrea said.
